holidays.name: World Tourism Day
holidays.description: A global day when people are encouraged to pack a bag, wander somewhere new, and remember that sitting in an airport eating overpriced pretzels counts as cultural exchange.
holidays.origin: Established in 1979 by the United Nations World Tourism Organization (UNWTO), with the date chosen to mark the anniversary of the adoption of the UNWTO Statutes in 1970.
holidays.funFact: Each year the day has a different theme, and a different host country holds the official celebrations.

holidays.name: National Chocolate Milk Day
holidays.description: A day to raise a frosty glass of cocoa-infused dairy and relive the glory of the cafeteria lunch line, this time with no one judging your milk mustache.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday, popularized by food-observance calendars and dairy fans, celebrating the sweet marriage of milk and chocolate.
holidays.funFact: Chocolate milk is often credited to Sir Hans Sloane, who in the late 1600s reportedly encountered cocoa in Jamaica and found it nauseating until it was mixed with milk.

holidays.name: Crush a Can Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the deeply satisfying crunch of flattening an empty aluminum can, combining stress relief with recycling responsibility.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance that encourages recycling by making it as fun as possible, since a crushed can takes up less space in the bin.
holidays.funFact: Aluminum cans can be recycled indefinitely, and a recycled can may be back on the store shelf in as little as 60 days.

holidays.name: National Corned Beef Hash Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble breakfast skillet of crispy potatoes and chopped corned beef, the ultimate leftover-fixing hero of diner menus everywhere.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance, born from the long tradition of turning leftover corned beef into a hearty second-act meal.
holidays.funFact: Canned corned beef hash became a staple of military rations and Depression-era kitchens because it was cheap, filling, and long-lasting.

holidays.name: Google Day
holidays.description: A day when the internet celebrates the search engine that taught us all to ask a machine questions we are too embarrassed to ask people.
holidays.origin: Google has marked September 27 as its birthday in many years, based on a date it used for celebrations, though the company was incorporated on September 4, 1998.
holidays.funFact: Google has celebrated its birthday on different dates over the years, including September 4, 7, 8, 26, and 27.
